Answer: B
Reason: The chest radiograph demonstrates a large, well-demarcated cystic lesion with an air-fluid level in the left lower lobe, which is a classic presentation of infected intralobar pulmonary sequestration. This finding aligns with the typical location (posterior basal segment of the left lower lobe) and radiographic appearance (cystic mass with fluid levels due to lack of normal bronchial drainage) for this condition.
